title: Privacy-first embedded video links with click-to-load and localized captions
context: Hunch Memory video series needed to be more discoverable to new users, but embedding YouTube iframes directly creates privacy and performance costs.
decision: Use youtube-nocookie.com with click-to-load pattern: embed thumbnail + play button, load iframe only on user click. Distribute video links across README, homepage, and docs with episode-specific links. Manage captions and ARIA labels through the locale generator for multi-language support.
consequences: No third-party tracking until user explicitly clicks to play
Reduced initial page load cost and network requests
Requires ongoing translation maintenance for video captions and ARIA labels
Adds lightweight client-side JavaScript to swap thumbnail for iframe on click
Video content is discoverable at multiple entry points (README, homepage, contextual docs sections)
alternatives_rejected: Direct iframe embedding: simpler but loads YouTube tracking immediately and requires page reload
Video links only in docs: less discoverable for new users or those reading README
English-only captions: excludes non-English users from guided learning
No click-to-load wrapper: trades privacy for simpler implementation
